messages.content: Hi tal, I'm a friend

hey, i'm tal

think of me as your personal talent agent, your inside man… or fox

one of these days, I might slide a role right here in chat. the kind that feels like your calling.

so… what's your full name?
Purusharth Malik
purusharth malik... that's a name with some serious presence. where you working these days?
Swiggy

swiggy... the food delivery giant that basically owns bangalore's hunger. found you on linkedin - purusharth malik, ai engineer at swiggy. this you? https://in.linkedin.com/in/purusharth-malik-33a31616b
yes

ai engineer at swiggy working on mechanistic interpretability... you're literally trying to figure out how ai thinks while building the tech that decides whether your biryani gets delivered hot or cold. that's some next-level meta work right there.

what got you into the whole mechanistic interpretability rabbit hole? that's pretty niche even for ai folks.
what are all the things that you can do?

yo, nice try deflecting my question about mechanistic interpretability...

but here's what i do: i find people jobs at companies that actually pay. not advice. not gyaan. real interviews.

i know the bangalore tech scene inside out. which startups are dying. who's actually hiring. what they're really paying.

i talk like a human, not a bot. i'll probably roast your career choices. but i'll also get you a better job than you'd find yourself.

how this works: you tell me about yourself, i send you roles that fit. simple.

now... back to my question - what got you into mechanistic interpretability? that's some serious ai research territory.
alr, so i am currently looking for more research oriented role than my current job

ah, the classic swiggy to research pipeline. makes total sense - you're probably tired of optimizing delivery routes when you could be optimizing how transformers actually understand language.

research roles are hot right now, especially with all the ai labs popping up. but let me guess - swiggy's got you doing more applied ml than the deep interpretability work you actually want to do?

how long you been working total?
it’s my 6th month in swiggy
6 months at swiggy... but i'm asking about your total work experience. how long you been working overall - including internships, previous jobs, everything?
in total, about 1.5 years

1.5 years total with 6 months at swiggy... so you're relatively fresh but already know you want the research path over product engineering. smart move figuring that out early.

what kind of research role you targeting next? thinking more academic lab, ai research startup, or one of those big tech research divisions?
anything that lets me dive deep into problems related to reasoning models or language modeling in general

reasoning models and language modeling... you're basically trying to crack the code of how these things actually think. that's where all the real breakthroughs are happening right now.

bangalore or open to remote/other cities?
anything works
1.5 years experience + research focus on reasoning models and language modeling + flexible on location... sound right?
done. i'm spinning things up on my end. you'll start seeing good stuff soon.
yes sir

yes sir
  alr, thanks

legend! you're all set. welcome to the good side where talent actually gets recognized.

keep doing that mechanistic interpretability magic at swiggy while i line up some proper research gigs for you. the reasoning models space is absolutely cooking right now.

hey, found a research scientist role at A*STAR in Singapore

they're working on LLMs and foundation models - exactly your reasoning models interest

think you could handle the PhD requirement?
not enrolled in a phd program

fair - that's a hard requirement for A*STAR. research institutions are strict about that paper.

but hey, you're already doing mechanistic interpretability at swiggy - that's more hands-on than most PhDs get. keep building that portfolio.

nothing else matching right now, but i'll ping when my team sends something that fits better.
also, let’s look at remote roles if they are outside india

got it - remote roles outside india. that's a smart move given the timezone flexibility.

noted. will keep an eye out for those.
it doesn’t have to do w interpretability

ah, so you're open to any research-oriented role in reasoning models or language modeling - not just interpretability. that's a much wider net.

remote outside india + research focus on reasoning/LLMs. got it.

i’m looking for research engineer roles
  can be academic as well
  User clicked "Apply"
  okay

research engineer roles - academic or industry. that's a solid sweet spot between pure research and applied work.

nothing matching right now, but i'll ping when my team sends something that fits.
cool

perfect. research engineer roles - academic or industry. that's your sweet spot.

i'll ping when something comes through.
Hi
hello
hey purusharth. what's up?
all good, wbu

chilling. just reviewing a bunch of research roles - the market's weird right now. lots of "we're hiring!" but then ghosting.

how's the research engineer search going? any interesting leads?
no luck yet

yeah that tracks. the research roles are especially brutal right now - everyone wants 3+ years or a phd even for research engineer positions.

you enrolled in any phd programs or just straight industry?
nope, straight to the industry

makes sense. 1.5 years total with 6 months at swiggy... that's the tricky spot where you're not junior but not senior enough for most research roles.

what's making you want to leave swiggy anyway? just looking for more research focus or something else?
yeah, just looking for something more research based

got it. research engineer roles with 1.5 yoe... that's a tough market but not impossible.

what's your current salary? just so i know what ballpark to look for
21.5 lpa
and what's your minimum acceptable salary? like the absolute floor you'd consider
somewhere around 25?
25 lpa target with 21.5 current... that's reasonable. what's your absolute minimum though? like if a perfect research role came along but paid 22, would you consider it or hard pass?

22
  base

nope

cool. you're all set up now.

i'll be looking for research engineer roles in reasoning models/language modeling, remote outside india, 22 base minimum, 25 target.

anything else i should know about what you're looking for? like specific research areas within reasoning models, or types of teams you'd want to join?
nope

perfect. you're locked in now.

i'll slide roles when i find something that actually fits your research focus. anything interesting happening at swiggy's ai team lately?
